Liquid Water in the Solar System

It would be nice if we had propulsion systems advanced enough to push an entire moon. Mars could be made much more earth-like if we could crash Europa or Titan into it. Not only would it increase the planets mass, the collision would heat the core, potentially creating a magnetic field more like the one on earth. On top of that the influx of water would also help to thicken the atmosphere.

Granted this would all take place over a geological time-period, but that should be expected when attempting to terraform a planet.

Mars could not be made more Earth-like in such a manner because Mars lacks a magnetic field and has a third of Earth's gravity. Any atmosphere would end up blown off by solar wind. In order to make Mars more Earth-like (to terraform it) we will need to build a massive magnetic shielding system in orbit to act as a deflector to knock those charged particle streams away from it.

As I said you increase the mass hence the gravitational field strength would also increase. I also addressed the magnetic field in that the collision would super heat the interior of the planet. We know that there is a lot of iron on Mars, that's why there the planet is red, from iron rust in the dust. If you can liquefy the core and there is a sufficient amount of iron, the planet may be able to generate a magnetic field similar to that of earth. That would prevent the new atmosphere from blowing away with the solar wind.

Physics does not work that way.

Firstly, slamming planetoids together isn't going to automatically make your masses perfectly additive. One could slam them together, but given their relative velocities and trajectories, there is significant chance for ejecta to be removed from the newly formed planetary system (as was the case for own planet's moon), especially in the realm of easy to convert to gaseous state materials such as ice. More importantly, as the two objects approach one another, depending on their structural composition, could result in tidal forces ripping one, the other, or both to bits. Thirdly, as the planetoids approach one another, they will begin to heat up, which would likely cause any ice on one of the moons to vaporize and either escape into space as the planet is fractured, or to cause a spectacular explosion, which would likely shatter significant portions of the inbound moon.

Now we can account for the easy stuff, like trajectory, impact forces, and system energy, we can't predict planetary structural behavior under those loads because they are infinitely more complex structural systems than we're used to designing an analyzing on Earth. In fact we don't even have a sufficient method to model our own planet for such circumstances, let alone our moon or two entirely other planetary objects.

Even if they did crash perfectly and masses were perfectly additive, you would have added no more than 3.5% the mass of Earth to Mars, leaving Mars at a paltry 14% the mass of Earth, increasing the gravitation field by a virtually insignificant value.

Second, assuming everything did go to plot and you crashed them together, there is zero guarantee that Mars' internal energy would rise to the point that it would kick start vulcanism. Yeah there's a good chance it would liquefy just about everything on the surface, crack the planet half open, and cause plenty of lava all over the place, but (once again) that doesn't mean it's going to follow your intended model. That is assuming that the core is solid iron, and if it wasn't and was already liquid, that would mean that Mars would always be unable to produce a magnetic field. Also, while Mars' surface regolith is comprised of around 2% iron oxide by weight, it would require the entirety of the surface of mars to reach 1250 C or 2280 F to convert that paltry amount of iron into metallic iron, which would then have to somehow seep all the way into the planet's core (obviously via volcanic subduction) without solidifying in the intervening rock strata layers, meaning the planet would have to be consistently heated to metallic iron's melting point, 1538 C or 2800 F.

Given that magma and lava (just the rock stuff, not the metals) is around 2400 F, that means the entire planet would become fluid in order for the metals to flow together, which there'd be no of knowing if it would, since temperature differentials would exist throughout the entire planet due the differences in material behavior and heat loss to space (what occurs on Earth).

Basically, you would need to revert the planet to it's primordial state, rendering it uninhabitable for tens of to hundreds of millions of years, rendering the entire endeavor completely pointless.

This is going to sound ridiculous, but I really hope for a real answer from any Voaters genuinely knowledgeable on the subject. So, here it is:

If an overweight or obese pregnant woman was to starve, how would it affect the child she was carrying? Would the fat in her body be converted into sustenance for the baby? What would the likelihood be of the baby being born healthy? Lastly, how do foetuses not get crushed by flat-out obese pregnant women, especially when they lie down?
Serious question(s) about obese pregnant women

My wife was pregnant last year. I think in the early stages one should not starve themselves. The beginning is very fragile. Towards the second and third trimester the woman's body (host) will provide for the baby as best it can. If the mother doesn't eat it will convert fat into energy for the child. If the baby needs more calcium than the mother provides, it will leach it from the mother's bones. Hence the importance of prenatal vitamins.

Not sure how the baby doesn't get crushed, but a pregnant woman's belly is very hard to protect the fetus.

Not a doctor, but my mom and sister are ob nurses. There's already a higher than average chance of miscarriage with fatty preggos, so my guess is that it would increase the chances even more. Leeching from the moms body can only do so much.

If an overweight or obese pregnant woman was to starve, how would it affect the child she was carrying?

Lack of nutrients would lead to birth defects, low birth weights, developmental problems. For example, spina bifida, which is caused by vitamin B deficiency. Every pregnant woman should take appropriate vitamin supplements, regardless of health.

Would the fat in her body be converted into sustenance for the baby?

Yes, but fat can only become a few select things through biosynthetic pathways, there would be other things missing that your body cannot produce like essential amino acids, most vitamins, etc.

What would the likelihood be of the baby being born healthy?

Depends on the duration of starvation and her weight. If she did not eat the entire pregnancy, even if she did have enough energy stored in her fat, she would die herself too of malnutrition. With the correct supplements, the baby would probably still have a really low birth weight but it might come out okay, maybe. But she would need to be so fat that the baby wouldn't be okay anyway.

Lastly, how do foetuses not get crushed by flat-out obese pregnant women, especially when they lie down?

Flat out obese pregnant women DO have pregnancy problems. Its actually very risky and they miscarry all the time. I don't know about crushed though. See what holds a lot of those squishier organs from getting crushed is basically fluid pressure. The fluid around the baby being in an enclosed sac of a certain size would keep the uterus from collapsing.

If an overweight or obese pregnant woman was to starve, how would it affect the child she was carrying?

It wouldn't affect much. Anecdotal evidence here but whatever.... during the first trimester I lost some weight, not much but only about 12 pounds. Before the pregnancy I was Obese Class III. During the second trimester, I kicked started my path to losing via CICO, MFP, and good ol' FPH for motivation (I seriously love that sub!). Lost about 40+ in total. Third Trimester, a switch flipped on my brain and suddenly I needed to eat everything in sight. Not wanting to undo all my progress, I ate very low calorie munchies. Gained back 20 pounds but about 7 of it was fat. Day I gave birth, I was only 20 pounds less than my pre-weight loss. 24 hours after birth, bye bye 12 pounds. Two weeks after, bye bye another 5 pounds. Didn't do anything, still ate the same amount I did when that 'switch' was flipped on, and I lost all the weight I regained and then some. Now I'm 4 months post partum and in the Overweight BMI category.

Imagine that, I went from Class III Obese to Class I Obese during the pregnancy. My OBGYN and other nurses told me that the whole "don't lose weight while pregnant/don't do diet" thing is mostly a response because hamplanets that have no IQ points would crash diet; Slim Fast diet, Water and Cayenne Pepper, Beach Body, etc. They all say that CICO is not a crash diet or a fad diet... and that as long as you get all your macros, micros, and take your prenatals while doing CICO, you are perfectly fine "starving yourself" during your pregnancy.

How it affected my kid? Well. He ended up being born at 7 pounds 7 ounces. No health complications. How did it affect my pregnancy? I had no problems. I was not in danger of pre-eclampsia, not in danger of gestational diabeetus, I had a low risk pregnancy. Everything was hunky dory and my blood pressure was normal, vitals were all normal too.

According to doctors, prenatals are for the moms only. The baby gets ALL of their nutrients from you. Doesn't matter if you're starving or eating junk, if baby needs calcium you can bet baby is gonna take it from your bones. The prenatals are to make sure that the mother gets HER nutrients incase there are days she can't fit all her macros and micros, that way Mom doesn't end up with deficiencies.

Would the fat in her body be converted into sustenance for the baby?

Yes.

What would the likelihood be of the baby being born healthy?

In my case, it was high. My doctors were happy I lost the weight instead of gained. Losing so much weight initially instead of gaining a lot, has helped my health immensely and the health of my baby.

Lastly, how do foetuses not get crushed by flat-out obese pregnant women, especially when they lie down?

In my case, the organs were shifted. My stomach was behind the fetus. Organs get shifted around during pregnancy to prevent it interfering with a growing baby. There were days my stomach was behind the baby, on top of the baby, or to the side of the baby. When I bend down, the pain was immense, because it was not only gravity pulling on the fetus but all the other organs too, hence why I completely stopped bending down while pregnant. The body is smart, it knows to prioritize the safety of the baby, it doesn't care if it has to CRUSH your organs to do it. Haha, stomach and bladder got squished, it wasn't fun but I dealt with it.
